q.s: A patient with severe liver disease has RBCs with projections of varying size at irregular intervals. These cells are:
e: Correct. Spur cells; also abetalipoproteinemia and vitamin E deficiency.

q.s: Teardrop cells (dacrocytes) on a peripheral smear suggest:
o: Bone marrow infiltration such as myelofibrosis
e: Correct. The cell "sheds a tear" as it is squeezed out of the marrow.

q.s: A patient with a mechanical aortic valve has hemolytic anemia. Which cells are expected on smear?
e: Correct. Fragmented "helmet" cells from mechanical hemolysis.

q.s: Bite cells (degmacytes) result from:
o: Splenic macrophages removing Heinz bodies in G6PD deficiency

q.s: Which conditions are associated with target cells?
o: HbC disease, asplenia, liver disease and thalassemia

q.s: Echinocytes (burr cells) are associated with:
o: End-stage renal disease and pyruvate kinase deficiency

q.s: Spherocytes have which surface area-to-volume ratio compared with normal RBCs?
e: Correct. Small, spherical cells without central pallor.

q.s: Hereditary elliptocytosis is caused by mutations in genes for:
o: RBC membrane proteins such as spectrin

q.s: Which factors precipitate sickling?
o: Low oxygen, acidosis, high altitude and dehydration

q.s: A patient with megaloblastic anemia would have which RBC shape on smear?
Ringed sideroblasts are seen in which sample and with which stain?
e: Correct. Perinuclear mitochondria with excess iron.

q.s: A 20-year-old with sickle cell disease has small basophilic nuclear remnants in RBCs. These are:
e: Correct. Seen in functional hyposplenia or asplenia.

q.s: Which RBC inclusion contains iron?
Heinz bodies require which stain to be seen?
o: Supravital stain such as crystal violet

q.s: Heinz bodies are composed of:
Basophilic stippling is seen in which conditions?
o: Sideroblastic anemias (including lead poisoning) and thalassemias

q.s: Howell-Jolly bodies are normally removed by:
Which mnemonic links Heinz bodies to bite cells?
Iron granules forming ringed sideroblasts are found in which cause of anemia?
e: Correct. Also lead poisoning and myelodysplastic syndromes.

q.s: HELLP syndrome causes which RBC morphology?

rounds.t: Anemia classification, iron studies, and iron deficiency

q.s: Which anemia is microcytic?
e: Correct. Microcytic causes: thalassemias, anemia of chronic disease, iron deficiency, lead (TAIL).

q.s: Which is a cause of nonmegaloblastic macrocytic anemia?
e: Correct. Also chronic alcohol use and Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

q.s: Normocytic hemolytic anemias have which reticulocyte response?
o: Normal reticulocyte index with low EPO

q.s: Which is an extrinsic cause of hemolytic anemia?
e: Correct. Also autoimmune, macroangiopathic and infections.

q.s: Which anemia results from defective DNA repair?
A patient with anemia has a reticulocyte count of 6% and an Hct of 22% (normal 45%), with a maturation time of 2. What is the reticulocyte production index?
An RPI below 2 indicates:
How is the Mentzer index calculated?
A patient with microcytic anemia has an MCV of 64 fL and an RBC count of 6.2 million/µL. The Mentzer index suggests:
e: Wrong. Not the use of the index.

q.s: Iron deficiency anemia shows which iron study pattern?
o: ↓ iron, ↑ TIBC, ↓ ferritin, markedly ↓ transferrin saturation

q.s: A 65-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has anemia. Which iron profile is expected?
A pregnant woman taking no supplements has normal serum iron and ferritin. Which iron study change is expected from pregnancy itself?
e: Correct. Pregnancy and OCPs raise transferrin.

q.s: Which is the primary iron storage protein in the body?
Why does the body lower circulating iron (low TIBC) in chronic inflammation?
o: To keep iron away from pathogens

q.s: In iron deficiency, which step of heme synthesis is decreased?
o: The final step (iron insertion into protoporphyrin)

q.s: A 30-year-old woman with heavy menstrual periods craves ice and has spoon-shaped nails. Which finding is expected?
e: Correct. Also ↑ RDW and low ferritin.

q.s: Which symptom is associated with iron deficiency?
e: Correct. Also pica, koilonychia, glossitis, cheilosis.

q.s: In iron deficiency anemia, which change in RBC appearance is typical?
Which is a common cause of iron deficiency in a 70-year-old man?
e: Correct. Must evaluate for colon cancer.

q.s: Which iron study pattern is seen in hemochromatosis?

rounds.t: Thalassemias, lead poisoning, and sideroblastic anemia

q.s: α-globin genes are located on which chromosome?
Deletion of one α-globin gene causes:
A patient with 3 α-globin genes deleted forms which abnormal hemoglobin?
e: Correct. Excess β chains form tetramers.

q.s: Hydrops fetalis incompatible with life results from:
Compared with iron deficiency, α-thalassemia trait typically has:
Cis deletion of two α-globin genes is more common in which population, and what is its significance?
o: Asian; offspring are at risk of more severe disease
All populations equally; no clinical effect
e: Wrong. Trans is more common in African ancestry.
Correct. Both deletions on one chromosome can pass together.

q.s: β-thalassemia results most often from which mutation type?
o: Point mutations in splice sites or the promoter (Kozak sequence)

q.s: β-thalassemia minor shows which electrophoresis finding?
A 9-month-old boy of Greek descent has severe anemia, hepatosplenomegaly and frontal bossing. Skull x-ray shows a "crew cut" appearance. Which genotype is most likely?
Why does β-thalassemia major become symptomatic around 6 months of age?
o: HbF declines as γ-chain production falls

q.s: A transfusion-dependent patient with β-thalassemia major develops diabetes, cardiomyopathy and skin darkening. Why?
Patients with β-thalassemia major have increased risk of aplastic crisis from which virus?
Lead inhibits which two enzymes of heme synthesis?
Why do RBCs show basophilic stippling in lead poisoning?
o: Lead inhibits rRNA degradation, so RBCs keep rRNA aggregates

q.s: A 3-year-old living in a house built in 1950 has abdominal colic, irritability and anemia. X-ray shows dense lines at the metaphyses of long bones. Which treatment is appropriate?
e: Correct. Chelation with succimer, EDTA or dimercaprol.

q.s: An adult battery factory worker develops wrist drop and blue-gray lines on the gums. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Burton lines and wrist/foot drop.

q.s: Which is the most common reversible cause of sideroblastic anemia?
e: Wrong. A cause, but not the most common.

q.s: A man taking isoniazid for latent TB develops microcytic anemia with ringed sideroblasts. What is the treatment?
e: Correct. B6 is the cofactor for ALA synthase.

q.s: Sideroblastic anemia shows which iron study pattern?
The genetic form of sideroblastic anemia involves an X-linked defect in which enzyme?
Megaloblastic anemia results from:
o: Impaired DNA synthesis delaying nuclear maturation relative to the cytoplasm

q.s: Which drug can cause megaloblastic anemia?
e: Correct. Also hydroxyurea, phenytoin, sulfa drugs and long-term metformin.

q.s: How can folate deficiency be distinguished from B12 deficiency by laboratory testing?
o: MCV is low in folate deficiency
Homocysteine is normal in folate deficiency
Neutrophils are normal in folate deficiency
Methylmalonic acid is normal in folate deficiency
Methylmalonic acid is high in folate deficiency

q.s: A 48-year-old man with alcohol use disorder and a poor diet has macrocytic anemia with hypersegmented neutrophils. He has no neurologic deficits. Methylmalonic acid is normal and homocysteine is high. Diagnosis?
Which spinal cord tracts are affected in subacute combined degeneration from B12 deficiency?
o: Dorsal columns, lateral corticospinal and spinocerebellar tracts

q.s: A patient with B12 deficiency is mistakenly treated with folate alone. What happens?
o: Anemia improves but neurologic symptoms worsen
Both anemia and neurologic symptoms resolve

q.s: Why does B12 deficiency from a vegan diet take years to develop?
o: The liver stores large amounts of B12
B12 is made by human cells
B12 is absorbed in the stomach rapidly
e: Correct. Folate deficiency develops in weeks to months.

q.s: A Finnish man who eats raw freshwater fish develops macrocytic anemia. Which organism is responsible?
e: Correct. Fish tapeworm competes for B12.

q.s: A 2-year-old has failure to thrive, developmental delay and megaloblastic anemia that does not respond to folate or B12. There is no hyperammonemia. Urine contains orotic acid. Treatment?
Orotic aciduria is distinguished from ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency by:
o: Presence of orotic acid in urine
e: Wrong. OTC is X-linked; orotic aciduria is AR.

q.s: Nonmegaloblastic macrocytic anemia differs from megaloblastic anemia by:
An 8-month-old has rapid-onset anemia, triphalangeal thumbs and short stature. HbF is elevated. White cells and platelets are normal. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Congenital pure red cell aplasia.

q.s: In anemia of chronic disease, which mediator increases hepcidin?
Hepcidin causes anemia of chronic disease by:
o: Binding ferroportin to block iron release from macrophages and gut cells

q.s: In a patient with chronic kidney disease and anemia of chronic disease, which therapy may be used?
Aplastic anemia shows which bone marrow finding?
A 25-year-old develops pancytopenia 2 months after acute hepatitis. Reticulocytes are low and EPO is high. Diagnosis?
Which drug is a classic cause of aplastic anemia?
e: Correct. Also benzene, alkylating agents and antimetabolites.

q.s: A 7-year-old boy has short stature, café-au-lait spots, absent thumbs and pancytopenia. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. AR DNA repair defect with marrow failure and cancer risk.

q.s: Which is a treatment for idiopathic aplastic anemia?

o: EMA binding test (decreased fluorescence) or osmotic fragility test

q.s: Hereditary spherocytosis shows which red cell index change?
e: Correct. Dehydrated cells with decreased surface area.

q.s: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria results from an acquired mutation in which gene?
e: Correct. Impaired GPI anchors for CD55 and CD59.

q.s: Which is the classic triad of PNH?
o: Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia and venous thrombosis

q.s: A patient with PNH develops abdominal pain, hepatomegaly and ascites. Which complication is most likely?
Eculizumab treats PNH by targeting:
An African American man develops back pain and dark urine 2 days after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Smear shows bite cells. Which enzyme is deficient?
e: Correct. X-linked; decreased NADPH and glutathione.

q.s: Why may G6PD activity be falsely normal during acute hemolysis?
o: The oldest, most enzyme-deficient cells have already lysed, leaving younger cells with more enzyme
The enzyme is induced by stress

q.s: Pyruvate kinase deficiency causes which change in hemoglobin oxygen affinity?
In sickle cell disease, what is the amino acid substitution in β-globin?
A 6-year-old with sickle cell disease has fever and bone pain in the femur. Which organism is classically associated with osteomyelitis in sickle cell disease?
e: Wrong. Septic arthritis in young adults.
Correct. Autosplenectomy increases risk from encapsulated organisms; Salmonella osteomyelitis is classic.

q.s: A 19-year-old with sickle cell disease has chest pain, fever, hypoxemia and new pulmonary infiltrates. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. A common cause of death.

q.s: Why do patients with sickle cell trait get hematuria?
o: Sickling in the low-Po2 renal medulla causes papillary necrosis

q.s: Which treatment raises HbF in sickle cell disease?
Homozygous HbC disease shows which smear finding?
o: Hemoglobin crystals inside RBCs and target cells

q.s: Which hemolytic anemia presents in a newborn with burr cells on smear?
e: Correct. Rigid RBCs from low ATP.
Wrong. Newborns are protected by HbF.
Wrong. Bite cells after oxidant stress.

rounds.t: Extrinsic hemolysis, leukopenias, porphyrias, and iron poisoning

q.s: A 32-year-old woman with SLE has hemolytic anemia with spherocytes and a positive direct Coombs test. Which antibody type is most likely responsible?
o: IgM with complement in the cold
e: Correct. Warm AIHA; "Warm weather is Good."

q.s: A 22-year-old with Mycoplasma pneumonia develops painful blue fingers in the cold and hemolytic anemia. Mechanism?
o: IgM and complement agglutinating RBCs in the cold

q.s: Which drug is classically associated with warm AIHA?
Cold AIHA is associated with which malignancy?
e: Correct. Also Mycoplasma and infectious mononucleosis.

q.s: On a smear, bite cells in a patient with drug-induced hemolysis suggest:
A pregnant woman at 35 weeks with severe hypertension has hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets. Which smear finding is expected?
e: Correct. HELLP is a microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.

q.s: Which condition causes macroangiopathic hemolytic anemia?
A traveler returning from Martha's Vineyard has hemolytic anemia with intraerythrocytic ring forms. Which organism is most likely?
e: Wrong. No travel to an endemic malaria area.

q.s: Neutropenia is defined as an absolute neutrophil count below:
e: Wrong. Severe infections occur below this.

q.s: Glucocorticoids cause which change in the white cell count?
Why do glucocorticoids cause neutrophilia?
o: They decrease neutrophil adhesion molecule activation, so neutrophils stay in the circulation
They destroy lymphocytes, which become neutrophils
They stimulate marrow production of eosinophils

q.s: Which is a cause of lymphopenia?
e: Correct. Also HIV, SCID, SLE, glucocorticoids, radiation.

q.s: Acute intermittent porphyria is caused by deficiency of which enzyme?
A 28-year-old woman has severe abdominal pain, weakness and anxiety after starting a barbiturate. Her urine darkens on standing. Which treatment is appropriate?
e: Correct. AIP; both decrease ALA synthase.

q.s: Which drugs precipitate attacks of acute intermittent porphyria?
e: Correct. They increase ALA synthase; alcohol and starvation do too.

q.s: A 50-year-old man with hepatitis C and heavy alcohol use has blistering lesions on the backs of his hands and tea-colored urine. Which enzyme is deficient?
e: Correct. Porphyria cutanea tarda, the most common porphyria.

q.s: Which treatment is used for porphyria cutanea tarda?
What is the rate-limiting step of heme synthesis?
A 2-year-old swallows several of her mother's prenatal iron tablets. She has vomiting, abdominal pain and bloody stools. X-ray shows radiopaque pills. Which treatment is indicated?
e: Correct. Chelation for acute iron poisoning.

q.s: Severe acute iron poisoning can progress to which acid-base disorder?
A mixing study is performed on a patient with prolonged PTT. The PTT corrects with normal plasma. This suggests:
e: Wrong. PTT is not a platelet test.

q.s: The most common acquired factor inhibitor is directed against:

Which treatment is used for hemophilia A?
o: Desmopressin, factor VIII concentrate or emicizumab

q.s: Vitamin K deficiency causes which coagulation pattern?
o: ↑ PT and ↑ PTT with normal bleeding time

q.s: Thrombin time is prolonged by:
e: Correct. Also anticoagulants and liver disease.

q.s: Which finding is common to all platelet disorders?
o: Increased bleeding time with mucosal bleeding and petechiae

q.s: A child has frequent nosebleeds, giant platelets on smear and mildly low platelets. Platelets fail to agglutinate with ristocetin, and adding normal plasma does not correct it. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Would correct with normal plasma.
Wrong. Not giant platelets with ristocetin defect.

q.s: A blood smear in Glanzmann thrombasthenia shows:
Immune thrombocytopenia most commonly involves antibodies against:
A bone marrow biopsy in ITP shows:
e: Correct. The marrow compensates for peripheral destruction.

q.s: Which is a TPO receptor agonist used for refractory ITP?
A patient with end-stage renal disease has prolonged bleeding after a dental extraction. Platelet count, PT and PTT are normal. Mechanism?
o: Uremic toxins impair platelet adhesion and aggregation

q.s: TTP is caused by:
o: Inhibition or deficiency of ADAMTS13, leaving large vWF multimers

q.s: A 4-year-old has bloody diarrhea after eating undercooked hamburger, followed by pallor, petechiae and decreased urine output. Smear shows schistocytes. PT and PTT are normal. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Shiga toxin–producing E. coli O157:H7.
Wrong. Adults, fever and neurologic symptoms.

q.s: How are TTP and HUS distinguished from DIC by laboratory testing?
o: PT and PTT are normal in TTP/HUS
e: Correct. The coagulation cascade is not activated.

q.s: A 35-year-old woman has fever, confusion, petechiae, anemia with schistocytes and rising creatinine. What is the treatment?
o: Plasma exchange with glucocorticoids and rituximab

q.s: Which feature distinguishes TTP from HUS?
e: Correct. TTP; HUS has bloody diarrhea.

q.s: Which is a cause of secondary ITP?
e: Correct. Also SLE, HCV, CLL and drugs.

rounds.t: von Willebrand disease, DIC, thrombophilias, and transfusion

q.s: A 16-year-old girl has heavy menstrual periods and frequent nosebleeds. Her mother has a similar history. Platelet count is normal, bleeding time is prolonged and PTT is mildly prolonged. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. The most common inherited bleeding disorder; mostly autosomal dominant.

q.s: Why is PTT prolonged in von Willebrand disease?
o: vWF carries and protects factor VIII
vWF is part of the extrinsic pathway

q.s: Which treatment is used for von Willebrand disease?
Which lab pattern is seen in DIC?
o: Normal PT and PTT with low platelets
Low platelets, prolonged PT and PTT, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer

q.s: A woman with placental abruption develops oozing from IV sites and hematuria. Which mnemonic lists the causes of this complication?
e: Correct. DIC causes include obstetric complications.

q.s: Which factors are decreased in DIC in addition to fibrinogen?

e: Wrong. No direct effect on PT.

q.s: A patient with nephrotic syndrome develops renal vein thrombosis. Which mechanism contributes?
o: Loss of factor VIII in urine

q.s: Factor V Leiden results from which mutation?
o: A 3′ untranslated region mutation increasing levels
Arg506Gln point mutation near the protein C cleavage site

q.s: A patient starting warfarin without heparin bridging develops painful, necrotic skin lesions on the thighs and breasts. Which deficiency is most likely?
Prothrombin G20210A mutation causes thrombosis by:
e: Correct. Mutation in the 3′ untranslated region.

q.s: One unit of packed RBCs raises hemoglobin by about:
A patient with hemorrhage and a fibrinogen of 60 mg/dL needs a product rich in fibrinogen and factor VIII. Which product?
e: Correct. Fibrinogen, VIII, XIII, vWF, fibronectin.

q.s: Prothrombin complex concentrate generally contains:
o: Factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S

q.s: Six hours after a plasma transfusion, a patient develops hypoxia, hypotension, fever and bilateral infiltrates without volume overload. Diagnosis?
A trauma patient receiving massive transfusion develops perioral numbness and a prolonged QT interval. Why?
o: Citrate in stored blood chelates calcium

q.s: Which electrolyte disturbance may result from transfusing old blood units?
e: Correct. RBCs lyse in old units.

q.s: Albumin infusion is used:
o: After large-volume paracentesis and during plasmapheresis

q.s: An elderly patient with heart failure develops dyspnea, hypertension and pulmonary edema during a rapid transfusion. Diagnosis?
Which is a classic cause of DIC?
e: Correct. Also trauma, snake bites, heat stroke, acute pancreatitis, APL.

rounds.t: Lymphomas, plasma cell dyscrasias, and myelodysplasia

q.s: Reed-Sternberg cells express which markers?
Which Hodgkin lymphoma subtype is the most common?
Which feature favors Hodgkin over non-Hodgkin lymphoma?
Which Hodgkin subtype has the worst prognosis?
e: Correct. "The poor have worse bank accounts."

q.s: A 12-year-old boy from equatorial Africa has a rapidly growing jaw mass. Biopsy shows a "starry sky" pattern. Which translocation is expected?
What is the most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults?

Mantle cell lymphoma involves overexpression of:
A gastric MALT lymphoma may regress with:
e: Correct. Marginal zone lymphoma with chronic inflammation.

q.s: A patient with AIDS has confusion and a single ring-enhancing brain lesion. Toxoplasma serology is negative and CSF is positive for EBV DNA. Diagnosis?
A man from Japan has skin lesions, lytic bone lesions and hypercalcemia. Which virus causes his lymphoma?
Mycosis fungoides is a type of:
e: Correct. Patches progressing to plaques and tumors.

q.s: A 68-year-old has back pain, anemia, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL and calcium 12.1 mg/dL. Urine dipstick is negative for protein. Which finding is expected?
o: Bence Jones proteinuria and "punched-out" lytic bone lesions

q.s: Why does multiple myeloma cause hypercalcemia?
o: Cytokines such as IL-1, TNF-α and RANK-L increase osteoclast activity

q.s: Rouleaux formation on a smear (RBCs stacked like poker chips) suggests:
A 70-year-old has headache, blurred vision and nosebleeds. Funduscopy shows dilated, sausage-shaped retinal veins. Serum protein electrophoresis shows an IgM spike. Diagnosis?
An asymptomatic 65-year-old has an M spike of 1.2 g/dL, no CRAB findings and 4% marrow plasma cells. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. 1–2% per year risk of myeloma.

q.s: Which complication of multiple myeloma involves deposition of light chains in tissues?
Myelodysplastic syndromes are distinguished from AML by:
Neutrophils with bilobed ("duet") nuclei in a patient with myelodysplastic syndrome are called:
A 4-year-old with Down syndrome has fever, bone pain, pallor and petechiae. Marrow shows numerous blasts that are TdT+ and CD10+. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Most common in children; Down syndrome association.

q.s: Which translocation in ALL indicates a better prognosis?
A teenager has a mediastinal mass with facial swelling and distended neck veins. Which leukemia is most likely?
e: Correct. Presents as a mediastinal mass with SVC-like syndrome.

q.s: A 72-year-old has lymphocytosis with smudge cells on smear. Flow cytometry shows CD5+, CD20+, CD23+ B cells. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. CD5+ but CD23−, cyclin D1.

q.s: A patient with long-standing CLL develops rapidly enlarging lymph nodes, fever and weight loss. This is called:
A 50-year-old man has massive splenomegaly and pancytopenia without lymphadenopathy. Bone marrow aspiration gives a dry tap. Cells have hairlike projections. Which treatment is used?
e: Correct. Purine analog for hairy cell leukemia (TRAP+, BRAF).

q.s: Auer rods are characteristic of:
A 40-year-old has fatigue, bleeding gums and DIC. Marrow shows abnormal promyelocytes with many Auer rods. Which treatment induces differentiation of these cells?
o: All-trans retinoic acid and arsenic trioxide

q.s: A patient with AML and a WBC count of 250,000/mm³ develops confusion and dyspnea. This is caused by:
e: Correct. Capillary occlusion by nondistensible blasts.

q.s: In a child with Down syndrome, which AML subtype is typical?
A 60-year-old has splenomegaly and WBC 120,000/mm³ with neutrophils, myelocytes, metamyelocytes and basophils. Which drug targets the causative protein?
e: Correct. CML with BCR-ABL from t(9;22).

q.s: A 55-year-old man has intense itching after hot showers and burning pain with red-blue color in his toes. Hct is 62% and EPO is low. Which mutation is most likely?
Which is a treatment for polycythemia vera?
A 70-year-old has massive splenomegaly, teardrop cells on smear and a dry tap on bone marrow aspiration. Which cytokine drives the marrow fibrosis?
Which myeloproliferative neoplasm presents with a markedly elevated platelet count with both bleeding and thrombosis, and normal RBC and WBC counts?
How is a leukemoid reaction distinguished from CML?
o: Leukemoid reaction has the Philadelphia chromosome
Leukemoid reaction has high LAP score; CML has low LAP and basophilia

q.s: A man with severe COPD has Hct 58%, low arterial O2 saturation and high EPO. This is:
A patient with a renal mass has Hct 60%, normal O2 saturation and high EPO. Classification?
e: Correct. EPO from renal cell carcinoma.

q.s: A 3-year-old has lytic skull lesions, a scaly scalp rash and recurrent otitis media. Biopsy cells are S-100+, CD1a+ and CD207+ with tennis-racket granules on EM. Diagnosis?
Translocations involving the Ig heavy chain gene on chromosome 14 cause cancer because:
o: The heavy chain gene is deleted
Oncogenes placed next to the constitutively active heavy chain region are overexpressed
